newsitem.title: BOSNIA: NATO formally launches new peace mission in Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: NATO formally launches new peace mission in Bosnia.

text.p: NATO on Friday formally launched a new multinational peacekeeping force in Bosnia with an 18-month mandate to police the peace agreement that ended the 43-month-long war.

NATO'S supreme commander in Europe General George Joulwan, handing over authority to soldiers of the 35,000-strong Stabilisation Force (SFOR) at a military ceremony, told them: "You are here to keep the peace not to fight a war.
The SFOR force, which will police the Dayton peace agreement reached in November 1995, took over from the Implementation Force (IFOR), a larger NATO-led army of 60,000.
The United States has offered 8,000 troops to the new force which sees the deployment of German combat troops for the first time since World War Two.
Despite being smaller, SFOR will fulfil a roughly similar mission to that of its predecessor.
Over the past year, NATO-led troops have successfully enforced military terms of the Dayton peace accords, separating Bosnia's rival armies and overseeing storage of heavy weapons.
Under the command of U.S. General William Crouch, SFOR will seek to ensure the armies continue to stick to the peace agreement, NATO officers said.

Carrying out the civilian side of the Dayton agreement has been much more difficult, with diplomats struggling to persuade former warring factions to form a peacetime government and to halt human rights abuses.
Western governments say the war could easily reignite in Bosnia without the continued presence of NATO troops patrolling former front lines.
Under the previous IFOR mission, British General Michael Walker commanded ground forces in Bosnia. But the Americans have taken direct command of ground forces in the new stabilisation force.
NATO ministers in Brussels have ruled out ordering the alliance troops to hunt down indicted war criminals still at large in Bosnia.
U.S. officials have suggested an international police force be set up outside of NATO to pursue war crimes suspects.
